newsitem.title: MEXICO: Dornbusch says Mexico pegging peso - report.
newsitem.headline: Dornbusch says Mexico pegging peso - report.

text.p: U.S. economist Rudiger Dornbusch said Mexico's central bank is pegging the peso exchange rate to fight inflation, hurting the export sector and economic growth, local newspaper Reforma reported on Tuesday.
But Mexican Finanace Minister Guillermo Ortiz denied to the newspaper that the peso exchange rate was being manipulated.

Dornbusch, a professor at the Massachussetts Institute of Technology, was quoted as saying, "it is wrong to say there is a free-floating currency in Mexico -- Banco de Mexico fixes it so it cannot move." He said the central bank "thereby assumes a wholly irresponsible attitude."
Dornbusch predicted the 1994 Mexican peso crash and was a professor to ex-Mexican finance minister Pedro Aspe.

"There was a problem last time, and they did not listen, and there will be another problem this time if in the coming months there is no move towards a real exchange rate policy," Reforma quoted Dornbusch as saying at a conference in Mexican Caribbean resort of Cancun.
The danger of this policy was that growth opportunities in the export sector were threatened, Reforma said.
Stock traders in Mexico said on Tuesday they had taken note of Dornbusch's comments.
"Many of us are concerned over the current exchange rate, that the peso is no longer a great advantage to exporting companies," a trader told Reuters.
Reforma also reported that Ortiz denied that the Mexican government was manipulating the peso, whose value, he said, is determined by market forces.

"The exchange rate is free-floating. By definition, the exchange rate cannot be manipulated one way or another," Ortiz was quoted as saying in Washington at an annual meeting of the World Bank and the International Monetary Fund.
